prompt: Review this Flipper app's app_free() for use-after-free and leaks.

result.text:
I can't review `app_free()` yet because the workspace has no source for it. A glob for `*.c`, `*.h`, `*.cpp`, `*.fam` and `*.py` found nothing, and a grep for `app_free` found no matches.

The only files here are the review skill's reference documents, so there is nothing to trace for use-after-free or leaks. I haven't guessed at the code or invented findings.

To go ahead, I need one of these:
- The path to the app's source, if it is somewhere outside this working directory.
- The code pasted here. `app_free()` plus the `app_alloc()` and struct definition would be the minimum. The timer, worker-thread, ViewPort and callback registrations matter most, because use-after-free in Flipper apps usually comes from a producer still running when teardown frees its state.

Once I have the code, I'll check these things:
- Which producers exist: timers, worker threads, GUI and input callbacks, UART/IRQ callbacks.
- Whether each producer is stopped and quiesced before the memory it touches is freed. `furi_timer_stop` doesn't wait for a running callback, so it doesn't count as quiescence.
- Whether any thread join happens while holding a lock the thread needs.
- Whether anything queued is drained before the queue is freed.
- Whether GUI and record handling is balanced: `view_port_enabled_set(false)` then `gui_remove_view_port`, `furi_record_close`, and view and dispatcher teardown order.
- Whether every allocation has a matching free, including on early-failure paths in `app_alloc()`.

Findings will be ranked by severity. Each will give the interleaving, the consequence, an evidence level (source trace or hypothesis), and a fix.
